📚 Today you learned

Buying Power vs. Net Liquidation Value

"Cash available" on a statement and real buying power aren't always the same number. Net liq is your account's total value right now — cash plus positions marked to market. Buying power is what you can actually deploy, and it lags reality whenever an order has filled but the record hasn't caught up — exactly today's situation with GOOG. If that $365 GTC buy already triggered against a stock trading in the $343-346 range, your real cash is ~$110 lower than the $542.01 portfolio.json shows, and you'd be carrying an unprotected position on top of it. This is why brokers, not spreadsheets, are the source of truth for cash — a tracking file can only be as current as its last sync. Forex margin accounts show this instantly with every tick; equities settlement and GTC order bookkeeping can lag by days, which is exactly the gap that's open right now.

Also today: Reg T buying power — in a margin account, buying power on marginable stocks is typically ~2x net liq, which is a separate multiplier on top of the cash-vs-net-liq gap above.
